question: 'Sange Meel Se Mulaqat' is the documentary of which famous musician?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Bismillah Khan**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Bismillah Khan** was a renowned Indian musician credited with popularizing the shehnai, a traditional Indian wind instrument.
 
• The documentary **'Sange Meel Se Mulaqat'** focuses on the life and musical journey of Bismillah Khan.
 
• Bismillah Khan received India's highest civilian honors, including the **Bharat Ratna** in 2001.
 
• He performed at the Red Fort on India's first Independence Day in 1947, marking the beginning of a tradition.
 
• Bismillah Khan's contribution to Indian classical music is celebrated globally, and he is remembered as a cultural icon.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Shehnai**

 
 
• The shehnai is a double-reed instrument traditional to India, often used in auspicious occasions and classical music.
 
• It is similar to the oboe and is known for its rich and soulful sound.
 
• Bismillah Khan is credited with elevating the shehnai from a folk instrument to one of classical status.
 
 
 
• **Bharat Ratna**
 
 
• It is the highest civilian award in India, instituted in 1954.
 
• The award recognizes exceptional service towards the advancement of art, literature, and science, and in recognition of public service of the highest order.
 
 
 
• **Indian Classical Music**
 
 
• It is divided into two major traditions: Hindustani (North Indian) and Carnatic (South Indian) music.
 
• Indian classical music is characterized by its raga (melodic framework) and tala (rhythmic patterns).
 
• Prominent instruments include the sitar, tabla, and shehnai.
 
 
 
• **Independence Day Performance**
 
 
• Bismillah Khan's performance at the Red Fort on August 15, 1947, is a historic moment in Indian history.
 
• His shehnai rendition signified the dawn of India's independence from British rule.
